messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I have a large dataframe (13k rows, 5k columns) that is grouped by a variable, npat.id <http://npat.id>. What I'd like to do is generate a dataframe with exactly the same variables, but with the mode of each variable by group within each output variable.

This works great in plyr, but is quite slow:

  # from http://stackoverflow.com/questions/2547402/standard-library-function-in-r-for-finding-the-mode
  Mode <- function(x, na.rm=T) {
    ux <- unique(x)
    if (na.rm) { ux = na.omit(ux)[1]}
    ux[which.max(tabulate(match(x, ux)))]
  }

  colmode <- function(x) { mode.result <- apply(x,2,Mode) }

  system.time(output.df <- ddply(df,.(npat.id <http://npat.id>),colmode,.progress="text"))

It works quicker if I use the parallel option in plyr. But it's still fairly slow (though much faster with ddply than sapply!).

I am a total newcomer to dplyr and can't seem to figure out the equivalent. Here's my best effort:

  output.df <-
    df %.%
    group_by(npat.id <http://npat.id>) %.%
    do(colmode(.))

Which starts things chugging (including a progress bar) but after some time I get

Error: Results are not data frames at positions: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8

In this case df is a 21 row, 5k column subset of the original for testing purposes, and there are 8 unique values of npat.id <http://npat.id>.

Perhaps the problem is how I generate the mode. I use the code I got from a great answer on Stack Overflow because I really do want to get the mode of each individual variable (grouped), no matter its type: character, numeric, etc. I just want to generate a dataframe of those mode "vectors" as the output.

Thanks in advance,

Boris Shor

In particular, I am trying to get the mode of every single variable organized by group. That is, I'm trying to reduce "subsets" of data frames with indeterminate numbers of rows to a single row, then reassemble the whole thing into a new data frame.

Here's reproducible code using plyr that works fine:

df = data.frame(npat.id <http://npat.id> = c(35,35,35,94,94,94), first = c("Mark","Mark","Mark","Ellen","Ellen","Ellen"), q16 = c(NA,1,1,0,NA,0), q33 = c(NA,0,0,0,1,0))

  npat.id <http://npat.id> first q16 q33
1      35  Mark  NA  NA
2      35  Mark   1   0
3      35  Mark   1   0

5      94 Ellen  NA   1
6      94 Ellen   0   0
>

# below from http://stackoverflow.com/questions/2547402/standard-library-function-in-r-for-finding-the-mode
 Mode <- function(x, na.rm=T) {
    ux <- unique(x)
    if (na.rm) { ux = na.omit(ux)[1]}
    ux[which.max(tabulate(match(x, ux)))]

Thank you in advance for any ideas; I'm sure its something obvious but I can't quite figure it out.

We have a challenge with a whole bunch of datasets that need summaries (sum, mean and length) calculated for all combinations of a bunch of dimensions, including the marginal totals. Hi all,

 unless I missed something, group_by() excepts the user to submit the grouping variables/expressions as arguments. This is very convenient in most case, but quite often, I have to group by columns from a separate list. This leads to awkward syntax like do.call(group_by, c(list(my_df), as.list(column.names))) or forces me to use the grouped_df() function, as in  grouped_df(my_df, as.list(column.names))

 It would be nice if one could have an optional parameter like

   group_by(my_df, group.vars = column.names)

In addition, it would also be useful to have some features of select() in group_by(), e.g.

  group_by(my_df, factor0:factor5)
  group_by(my_df, -x, -y)

Thanks!

-- t.

2 2 A
3 3 B
4 4 C
5 5 B
6 6 D
7 7 E

What I would like would like a third column with the values (1, 1, 2, 3, 3, 4, 5) that counts the number of distinct values of X that have been shown up through row t.

I tried:

d %.% mutate(cum_num_items = length(unique(X[1:t])))

But that just gets a column of 1's.   I'd like to be able to do this within mutate because I have to do it for sequences belonging to many different subjects.  Anyone know of a way to do this?

Andrew
